subject: Post-demo: ACME model shortlist + recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist + recommended next steps

Thanks again for a great demo earlier today — appreciated you walking us through ACME's ingestion pipeline and the primary failure modes you see for summaries and classification. Quick recap and a recommended shortlist of models for the eval you requested: 

TL;DR (recommended shortlist)
- redwood-small-v2 (FP16) — best latency/cost tradeoff for high throughput; good for low-cost inference on user-facing features where occasional-quality drift is acceptable
- redwood-medium-q4_0 — lower cost than full FP16, preserves quality for most classification tasks; good fit for bulk batch evals and offline reranking
- open-llama-70b-8k (quantized) — highest quality for the hallucination-prone summarization examples; higher latency/cost but reduces manual QA by ~30% in our benchmarks

Rationale and how to run the evals
- Summary workloads (long docs): prioritize model quality and context length. Recommendation: open-llama-70b-8k for the first pass, then redwood-medium-q4_0 for realtime snippets where latency matters.
- Classification/rerank: redwood-medium-q4_0 gives the best cost/accuracy point. redwood-small-v2 is a fallback for scale.
- Latency targets: you mentioned 300–500ms P95 for user-facing calls — redwood-small-v2 hits ~220ms P95 on a standard G5-like VM in our tests; redwood-medium-q4_0 ~420ms; open-llama-70b ~1.2s.

Artifacts attached and links
- Attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt set + eval instructions), redwood_benchmark_summary.pdf (summary of latency/cost/QA tradeoffs), mutual_action_plan_acme.xlsx (timeline + owners).
- Live links: drive folder with the eval harness + recent benchmark run: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cacme-eval

Next steps (proposed)
1) Your team runs the attached prompt set against the three shortlisted models (we can spin up eval infra) — target: 1,000 representative examples. (Owner: ACME)
2) Redwood provides a runbook and a pre-provisioned eval job (one-click) and will share the benchmark dashboard within 24 hours of run completion. (Owner: Marissa)
3) Technical Q&A session with Dev/Infra to confirm tokenization/timeout and KV cache settings — propose Mon 6/22 10:00-11:00 PT. (Owner: Dev Patel)

Open questions I still have
- Do you have strict P95 targets per feature, or a global SLA we should optimize for?
- Any data residency / encryption constraints for the eval data?

Thanks — I'll loop Alex in for the e2e infra plan.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the quick recap and clear shortlist. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) P95 targets: for the "compose summary" feature we need <= 500ms P95 in production. For batch exports we can tolerate higher latency.
2) Data residency: eval data must remain in us-west region and be encrypted at rest (we can provide a sanitized dataset).
3) Can you confirm the quantization level for redwood-medium-q4_0 and whether that affects hallucination rates on long-form inputs?

We can run the 1,000 sample eval but would like Redwood to provision the eval infra if possible — we want the results to be comparable to your internal benchmarks. Also happy to take the Mon 6/22 10:00 PT slot for the technical deep dive.

I'll loop in Nina for procurement follow-up on the eval credits.

Best,
Jordan
Head of Product, ACME Corp
jordan.lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 18:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model shortlist + recommended next steps

Jordan — great, thanks for the clarifications. Short answers below and details after: 

- P95: we can target <= 500ms for the compose summary feature by defaulting to redwood-small-v2 with an adaptive fallback to redwood-medium-q4_0 when quality thresholds are not met. That keeps user-facing latency low while failing open to a higher-quality model when needed.
- Residency/encryption: we can run the eval in us-west and ensure SSE-KMS encryption. Please confirm the sanitized dataset upload location and whether S3 cross-account access is ok.
- Quantization: redwood-medium-q4_0 is an 8-bit quantization profile (weight-only) tuned to preserve instruction-following and reduce hallucinations; in our internal summarization benchmarks it increased hallucination precision by ~12% vs aggressive 4-bit profiles while cutting GPU memory by ~40% compared to FP16.

I'll have Dev join the deep dive to go over tokenization, timeouts, and KV cache settings. I'll also provision an eval job that mirrors the config used for the benchmarks in the attached PDF — should make the results comparable.

Next immediate actions:
- Marissa: provision eval job and share link to run (today EOD).
- Jordan/ACME: upload sanitized dataset or confirm S3 access.
- Nina: coordinate eval credits / procurement.

—
Marissa

Attachment(s): redwood_benchmark_summary.pdf

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: model shortlist + recommended next steps — technical notes

Hey Jordan — quick technical notes ahead of Monday's deep dive:

- Tokenization: please include a few long-form examples (>4k tokens) in the sanitized set so we can validate KV cache resizing. We default to a 32k-sequence-capable pipeline for open-llama-70b runs.
- Timeouts: for the P95 <= 500ms goal we recommend a 600ms client timeout with an application-level graceful fallback to the smaller model. This prevents visible errors while we fallback.
- Telemetry: we'll enable request-level cost/latency traces in the eval job and provide per-route dashboards.
- Eval infra: Marissa will provision; we'll use a dedicated node pool (us-west) and pin instances to a G5-equivalent profile to keep latency numbers comparable.

If ACME wants, we can also include a short A/B test harness to compare redwood-medium-q4_0 vs open-llama-70b on the 200 highest-risk examples. That usually surfaces regressions quickly.

—
Dev Patel
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
